 ATP Basel Day 1 Predictions Including Dominic Stricker vs Casper Ruud 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 As the European season hurtles toward its final curtain, ATP Basel’s indoor hard courts become the ultimate proving ground. With ranking points precious and year-end ambitions on the line, the Swiss Indoors Basel  draws a hungry field and day 1 is stacked indeed. Under the closed roof, every rally carries extra weight: this is where seasons are salvaged, breakthroughs are born, and reputations are forged before the winter break. We bring you our predictions for every match on the schedule, who do you back to make the next round?
 ATP Basel Day 1 Predictions
 Valentin Vacherot vs Mariano Navone
 Head-to-Head: Vacherot 1–1 Navone
 Vacherot and Navone have split their two previous meetings, setting up an intriguing contest at ATP Basel between the Monegasque’s attacking game and the Argentine’s baseline consistency. Vacherot won their Miami meeting in straight sets earlier this year, but Navone responded with a three-set victory in Montreal. Their latest encounter suggests there is little to separate them when both find their rhythm.
 Basel’s indoor conditions should suit Vacherot’s ability to take the ball early and dictate with his groundstrokes. Navone will look to extend rallies and draw errors, but he could struggle if Vacherot controls the tempo from the start. The Argentine has already shown he can trouble his opponent, although the quicker surface gives Vacherot an opportunity to impose himself.
 Prediction: Vacherot in 3
 Holger Rune vs Quentin Halys
 Head-to-Head: Rune 2–0 Halys
 Holger Rune  has won both previous meetings, giving him a useful psychological advantage heading into this matchup. However, the Dane’s ability to turn that record into another victory will depend on how effectively he handles Halys’s first-strike tennis. The Frenchman possesses a powerful serve and can make life uncomfortable for opponents when he finds his range.
 If Rune can extend points and expose Halys’s movement, his greater tactical variety should prove decisive. The head-to-head record supports that view, but this could still be a competitive opener.
 Prediction: Rune in 3
 Daniel Altmaier vs Juan Manuel Cerundolo
 Head-to-Head: Cerundolo 3–0 Altmaier
 Cerundolo has enjoyed the better results in this matchup, including a straight-sets victory over Altmaier in Basel qualifying. That recent result gives the Argentine confidence, although a repeat encounter would present a different challenge if Altmaier can make adjustments.
 Altmaier is capable of constructing points patiently and using his consistency to frustrate opponents. Cerundolo, meanwhile, will look to take control from the baseline and continue exploiting the patterns that have worked in their previous meetings. The German needs a stronger start and greater efficiency on important points to reverse the trend.
 Given Cerundolo’s recent success against Altmaier, there is little reason to overlook the Argentine’s chances. His confidence in this matchup could be crucial.
 Prediction: Cerundolo in 2
 Mika Brunold vs Nuno Borges
 Head-to-Head: first meeting
 Aug 8, 2026; Montreal, QC, Canada; Nuno Borges (POR) hits a forehand against Luciano Darderi (ITA) during round of sixteen play at IGA Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images 
 This would be a significant test for Swiss player Brunold against the more experienced Borges. Playing at home can provide an extra lift, but Brunold would need to bring his best tennis to challenge an opponent accustomed to the demands of the ATP Tour.
 Borges is generally comfortable building points from the baseline, using his movement and consistency to make opponents work for openings. Brunold will need to serve effectively and take his chances when he gets opportunities to attack. If he allows Borges to settle into long rallies, the Portuguese player’s experience should give him the upper hand.
 Brunold’s familiarity with the local conditions could help him make the match competitive, but Borges has the more established record at this level.
 Prediction: Borges in 2
 Dominic Stricker vs Casper Ruud
 Head-to-Head: Ruud 1–1 Stricker
 Stricker has the advantage of home support and a game that could be particularly effective on Basel’s indoor hard courts. His left-handed serve and aggressive shot-making give him the tools to take time away from Ruud, especially if he can dictate early in rallies and avoid being pushed too far behind the baseline. The Swiss player will need to serve consistently and take his chances when openings appear.
 Ruud’s greater experience makes this a demanding test, but Stricker’s previous Basel victory offers a convincing blueprint. With the conditions in his favour and the confidence of having beaten Ruud here before, the Swiss player has a real opportunity to repeat the result.
 Prediction: Stricker in 3
